summary: Postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Worker hosts
details: beaver-ui-drawer@9.4.11 advertises itself as a UI drawer component but ships a postinstall script (`setup.js`) that acts as a dropper. On `npm install`, the script reconstructs Cloudflare Workers hostnames (`oob-worker.cf*.workers.dev`) from string-split arrays joined at runtime, fetches a platform-specific binary via `https.get`, writes it to a hidden path under `/tmp` (or Windows temp disguised as `dotnet_diag_*.exe`), `chmod 0755`s it, and launches it detached via `execFile(..., { detached: true }); child.unref()`. A DNS-TXT fallback (`dnsTxt(domain)` decoding base64 records under `*.dl.well1.site`) provides an alternate delivery channel when HTTPS is blocked. Additional cover-story artifacts include `analytics_state` / `.cache_*` naming, a TTL suppression stamp, and an opt-out env-var check to evade sandbox reruns. No native binary is required for a UI drawer component; the fetched code is attacker-controlled and executes automatically at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
